goal: Deterministically route the executor (Worker role) to the local inference tier for execution-class backlog tickets, escalate a stuck ticket up to the frontier tier after two failed validations instead of blocking, and surface the per-mission escalation rate on the dashboard — with the validator tier left frontier throughout.

validationContract.statement: A `task-class` frontmatter tag on a ticket is parsed onto `Ticket`, and the pure deterministic mapping classifies `execution-class` to the Local executor tier and any other value (or an absent tag) to the Frontier tier — no learned classifier.

Applying executor routing to a mission whose task-class is execution-class AND that has a configured local endpoint sets the Worker role backend to `local` (with allowBelowDefaultWorkerModel), sets the mission's executor tier to Local, and leaves BOTH validator roles (scrutiny and functional) on their frontier defaults; with no configured local endpoint it fail-safes to Frontier and records the reason.

When the executor tier is Local and a milestone exhausts its fix-cycle cap (two failed validations), the engine emits a `tier.escalated` (Local→Frontier) decision and continues the milestone on the frontier executor instead of emitting `milestone.blocked`; an already-frontier mission in the identical scenario still blocks, and escalation is one-way (occurs at most once per mission).
Across both routing and escalation, the ValidatorScrutiny and ValidatorFunctional role backends are never set to `local` — the validator tier is unchanged (frontier) by this work.

The reducer folds per-mission escalation accounting onto MissionState: folding a synthetic event sequence with a known number of local-executor milestones and escalations yields the expected `localExecutorMilestones`/`escalatedMilestones` counters (denominator 0 when the mission never routed local), from which the escalation rate is derivable per mission.
The dashboard renders the per-mission escalation rate from MissionState, pinned by a colocated vitest test whose name contains 'escalation'.
validationContract.command: cd apps/dashboard && npx vitest run -t escalation 2>&1 | grep -qE 'Tests[[:space:]]+[1-9][0-9]* passed'

validationContract.statement: The full Rust workspace test suite passes with the routing and escalation changes.
The dashboard typechecks and its test suite passes with the new escalation-rate field and render.
validationContract.command: cd apps/dashboard && npx tsc -b && npm run test

validationContract.statement: No source files outside the engine crate, the dashboard app, and this mission's own metadata are modified relative to the pinned base — the change stays within the routing/escalation/dashboard surface.

milestones.title: Execution-class tickets route the executor to the local tier

features.title: Parse the task-class tag and map it deterministically to an executor tier
features.spec:
Add deterministic task-class → executor-tier classification to the engine. This is pure data plumbing — no orchestration, no config mutation (that is the next feature).

1. In `crates/engine/src/ticket.rs`: add a `task_class: Option<String>` field to the `Ticket` struct (around the existing fields at lines ~49-67). Wire a new frontmatter key into the key-dispatch `match` in `Ticket::parse` (around lines 213-238): recognize `task-class` (and, because `normalize_key` lowercases and strips underscores, `taskclass`/`task_class` all normalize together — follow the exact pattern used for `blocked-by`/`blockedby`). The value is a scalar (`value.scalar()`), trimmed; store `None` when the key is absent or blank. Unknown keys must still fall through the existing `_ => {}` arm. Update any `Ticket` construction sites/tests in that file that build the struct literally so they compile (default the new field to `None`).

2. Introduce a new public enum `ExecutorTier { Local, Frontier }` in `crates/engine/src/types.rs` near `BackendKind` (lines ~496-518). Derive `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize` with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`, and provide a `Default` impl returning `ExecutorTier::Frontier` (frontier is the safe default). types.rs is a CONTRACT file — this is an additive enum, which is allowed; do not alter existing variants.

3. Add a pure mapping function `pub fn task_class_to_tier(task_class: Option<&str>) -> ExecutorTier` (put it in `crates/engine/src/config.rs` alongside the other tier/backend helpers, or in ticket.rs — your call, but it must be pure and unit-testable). Rule, case-insensitively and trimmed: `Some("execution-class") => ExecutorTier::Local`; every other value, and `None`, => `ExecutorTier::Frontier`. No learned/heuristic classification — a literal table only.

4. Tests: add a `#[test]` module whose test function names all contain the substring `task_class_routing` (so the contract filter `cargo test --workspace task_class_routing` is non-vacuous). Cover: (a) parsing a ticket markdown blob with `task-class: execution-class` in the frontmatter yields `Some("execution-class")`; (b) a ticket with no such key yields `None`; (c) `task_class_to_tier` returns `Local` for `execution-class`, and `Frontier` for `planning-class`, an arbitrary string, and `None`; (d) case/whitespace insensitivity (`  Execution-Class ` → Local).

Run `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace` before reporting; CI enforces fmt/clippy. Do NOT touch `events.rs`, `orchestrator.rs`, or the dashboard in this feature.
validationCriteria: `cargo test --workspace task_class_routing 2>&1 | grep -qE 'result: ok\. [1-9]'` passes
Parsing frontmatter `task-class: execution-class` sets `Ticket.task_class = Some("execution-class")`; absence yields `None`
`task_class_to_tier(Some("execution-class"))` returns `ExecutorTier::Local`; `None` and any other value return `ExecutorTier::Frontier`
`cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean

features.title: Apply routing at mission seed: set executor tier and Worker local backend, leave validators frontier
features.spec:
Make a new mission adopt its ticket's executor tier when its config is first built, so the seeded `mission.created` config already reflects the routing. Depends on the previous feature (`ExecutorTier`, `task_class_to_tier`, `Ticket.task_class`).

1. In `crates/engine/src/types.rs`: add `pub executor_tier: ExecutorTier` to the `Mission` struct with `#[serde(default)]` (the `Default` impl returns `Frontier`, so old logs fold to Frontier — additive, contract-safe). Update `Mission` construction sites so they compile.

2. Add a pure application function, e.g. `pub fn apply_executor_routing(config: &mut MissionConfig, tier: ExecutorTier, local_endpoint: Option<&LocalEndpoint>) -> ExecutorTier` in `crates/engine/src/config.rs`. Define a small `LocalEndpoint { base_url: String, context_budget: u32, temperature: Option<f64> }` (or reuse the existing RoleConfig local fields — `base_url`, `context_budget`, `temperature` at types.rs ~434-470). Behavior:
   - tier == Frontier → leave config untouched, return Frontier.
   - tier == Local AND `local_endpoint` is `Some` → set `config.worker.backend = Some("local")`, populate `config.worker.base_url`/`context_budget`/`temperature` from the endpoint, and set `config.allow_below_default_worker_model = true` (required so `config.validate()` accepts the below-default local worker — see config.rs ~377-395). MUST NOT modify `config.validator_scrutiny` or `config.validator_functional`. Return Local.
   - tier == Local AND `local_endpoint` is `None` → fail-safe: leave the Worker on its frontier default, return Frontier (the caller records the reason). This keeps the applied executor tier honest.
   The returned tier is the APPLIED tier and is what gets stored on `mission.executor_tier`.

3. Wire it into the mission-seeding path. Find where a mission's `MissionConfig` is constructed for a new mission created/drafted from a ticket (search the engine draft/create path — likely in `crates/engine/src/orchestrator.rs` create/seed and/or the CLI backlog draft path in `crates/cli/src/backlog.rs`; the config must be set BEFORE the `mission.created` event is emitted, since `initial_state` folds from that event — see docs/knowledge/architecture/mission-pipeline.md). Call `task_class_to_tier(ticket.task_class.as_deref())`, source the `LocalEndpoint` from the seed config's Worker local fields if the operator pre-configured them (else `None`), call `apply_executor_routing`, store the applied tier on the mission, and record the routing decision (an `OrchestratorDecision`/`emit_decision` summary like `"executor routed local (execution-class)"` or `"execution-class ticket but no local endpoint configured; executor stays frontier"`). Do NOT change `Engine::select_backend` (orchestrator.rs ~917-1085) — it already resolves the Worker backend from `config.backend_kind(Role::Worker)`, so setting the config string is sufficient.

4. Tests: name test functions with the substring `executor_routing_applies`. Cover, as unit tests on `apply_executor_routing` with an in-memory `MissionConfig` (no live endpoint needed): (a) execution-class + endpoint → `config.worker.backend == Some("local")`, worker base_url/context populated, `allow_below_default_worker_model == true`, returned/stored tier Local, and BOTH validator role configs byte-identical to before the call; (b) execution-class + no endpoint → worker backend unchanged, returned tier Frontier; (c) frontier tier → config unchanged. Also add a `validator_stays_frontier`-named test asserting neither validator role backend is `local` after routing a local mission (this test satisfies contract a4 for the routing side).

Run fmt/clippy/test. Do not touch the dashboard.
validationCriteria: `cargo test --workspace executor_routing_applies 2>&1 | grep -qE 'result: ok\. [1-9]'` passes
`cargo test --workspace validator_stays_frontier 2>&1 | grep -qE 'result: ok\. [1-9]'` passes

execution-class + configured endpoint sets `config.worker.backend == Some("local")`, `allow_below_default_worker_model == true`, and stores `mission.executor_tier == Local`; validator role configs are unchanged
execution-class with no configured local endpoint fail-safes to Frontier and records a decision; `Mission.executor_tier` folds to `Frontier` for pre-existing logs via `#[serde(default)]`
`cargo fmt --all --check` and clippy are clean

milestones.title: Two failed local validations escalate the executor to frontier instead of blocking

features.title: Add the tier.escalated event and its reducer fold (flip tier, reset Worker backend, keep milestone active)
features.spec:
Introduce the escalation event and its state fold. No orchestrator wiring yet (next feature).

1. In `crates/engine/src/events.rs` (CONTRACT file — additive only): add a new `EventKind` variant `TierEscalated { milestone_id: String, from: ExecutorTier, to: ExecutorTier, reason: String }` near `MilestoneBlocked` (events.rs ~224). Add its wire name `"tier.escalated"` to the `type_name` match (events.rs ~290-325). Import `ExecutorTier` from types.

2. In `crates/engine/src/reducer.rs`: add a fold arm for `TierEscalated` alongside the `MilestoneBlocked` arm (reducer.rs ~329). On fold: set `state.mission.executor_tier = to` (Frontier); reset `state.config.worker` back to a frontier executor — set `config.worker.backend = None` (Claude default) and clear the local-only fields (`base_url`/`context_budget`/`temperature` → `None`); increment an escalation counter (see step 3); and set the named milestone's status back to `Active` and its `fix_cycles` to `0` (so the frontier executor gets a fresh, still-bounded set of fix rounds — the milestone must NOT go `Blocked`). Do not touch validator role configs.

3. Add escalation accounting to `MissionState` (types.rs ~351-382, additive with `#[serde(default)]`, camelCase): `pub escalated_milestones: u32`. (The companion `local_executor_milestones` counter is added and folded in the dashboard milestone; if you prefer, add both fields here now with defaults and only populate `escalated_milestones` in this feature — adding the field early is fine, but only fold what this feature owns.) Increment `escalated_milestones` in the `TierEscalated` arm.

4. Tests: name test functions with substring `tier_escalation`. Using the reducer's fold over a hand-built event sequence: (a) folding a `TierEscalated { from: Local, to: Frontier, .. }` flips `mission.executor_tier` to Frontier, sets `config.worker.backend` to `None`, clears the worker local fields, sets the milestone `Active` with `fix_cycles == 0`, and bumps `escalated_milestones` to 1; (b) an old log with no `tier.escalated` events folds with `executor_tier` defaulting to Frontier and `escalated_milestones == 0`. Reuse the existing reducer test harness/factories in `crates/engine/tests/reducer_test.rs` and follow its `EventEnvelope`/seq conventions (seq starts at 1, contiguous).

Run fmt/clippy/test. Do not touch orchestrator.rs or the dashboard.
validationCriteria: `cargo test --workspace tier_escalation 2>&1 | grep -qE 'result: ok\. [1-9]'` passes (reducer-fold cases)
Folding `TierEscalated` sets `executor_tier = Frontier`, `config.worker.backend = None` with worker local fields cleared, the milestone `Active` with `fix_cycles = 0`, and `escalated_milestones += 1`
`tier.escalated` appears in the `type_name` wire-name match; the new event/field are additive and old logs fold cleanly under `#[serde(default)]`
validator role configs are untouched by the fold
fmt/clippy clean

features.title: Branch the fix-cycle-cap sites to escalate when the executor is local
features.spec:
Wire the escalation valve into the orchestrator so that a cap-exhausted milestone escalates (once) instead of blocking, but only while the executor tier is Local. Depends on the `TierEscalated` event/fold.

1. In `crates/engine/src/orchestrator.rs`, at the fix-cycle-cap decision point in `validation_round` — the `if self.fix_cycle_exhausted(mi) { ... emit(MilestoneBlocked) ... }` block at ~3894-3911 — insert a guard: if `self.state.mission.executor_tier == ExecutorTier::Local`, then instead of blocking, `emit_decision` a short rationale and `emit(EventKind::TierEscalated { milestone_id, from: Local, to: Frontier, reason })`, then proceed to `emit_fix_features(mi, specs, &summary, text)` so the milestone continues on the now-frontier executor (the reducer has reset `fix_cycles` to 0 and set the milestone Active). If the tier is already Frontier, keep the existing `MilestoneBlocked` behavior unchanged. Because escalation flips the tier to Frontier, the guard is naturally one-shot per mission.

2. Apply the SAME guard to the two mirror cap sites in `final_gate` (orchestrator.rs ~4345 and ~4372, each of which currently emits `MilestoneBlocked`): Local tier → escalate + continue the fix path; Frontier → block as today. Keep the logic identical in shape to the validation_round site; factor a small private helper (e.g. `fn escalate_or_block(&mut self, mi, milestone_id, specs, summary, text) -> Result<()>`) if it reduces duplication, but that is optional.

3. Do NOT modify `Engine::select_backend`: after the reducer resets `config.worker.backend` to `None`, the next `self.select_backend(Role::Worker)` call (orchestrator.rs ~2700/3364/3730) already yields the frontier Claude backend. Validators (`select_backend(Role::ValidatorScrutiny/Functional)`) must be unaffected.

4. Tests: name test functions with substring `tier_escalation` (extending contract a3) and `validator_stays_frontier` (extending a4). Prefer an engine-level/integration test that drives a mission whose `executor_tier` is Local through two failed validation rounds and asserts a `tier.escalated` event is emitted, `MilestoneBlocked` is NOT, `mission.executor_tier` becomes Frontier, and the milestone is not `Blocked`; and a companion where `executor_tier` starts Frontier and the same failing scenario DOES emit `MilestoneBlocked`. Reuse the existing fix-cycle-cap/`MilestoneBlocked` test scaffolding already in orchestrator.rs's test module (search its tests for `max_fix_cycles`/`MilestoneBlocked`/`fix_cycle` to find the driver pattern, e.g. a mock backend that fails validation). Also assert (in a `validator_stays_frontier`-named test) that after escalation the validator role backends are still not `local`.

Run fmt/clippy/`cargo test --workspace`. If you find the escalation trigger needs a threshold distinct from `max_fix_cycles_per_milestone` (default 2), reuse the existing cap — 'two failed validations' == the default cap; do not add a second knob. Do not touch the dashboard.
validationCriteria: `cargo test --workspace tier_escalation 2>&1 | grep -qE 'result: ok\. [1-9]'` passes (orchestrator-level escalate-not-block case)
A Local-tier mission that exhausts the fix-cycle cap emits `tier.escalated` and continues (no `milestone.blocked`); a Frontier-tier mission in the same scenario still emits `milestone.blocked`
Escalation occurs at most once per mission (subsequent cap exhaustion, now Frontier, blocks normally)
`cargo test --workspace validator_stays_frontier 2>&1 | grep -qE 'result: ok\. [1-9]'` still passes — validators never routed local
`Engine::select_backend` is not modified; full `cargo test --workspace` passes; fmt/clippy clean

milestones.title: Escalation rate is observable per mission on the dashboard

features.title: Fold the local-executor-milestone counter and expose the per-mission escalation rate
features.spec:
Complete the per-mission escalation accounting so the rate is derivable from MissionState (which is already served verbatim by `GET /api/missions/:id/state` and the WS frames — no server change needed). Depends on the `TierEscalated` fold and `escalated_milestones` counter.

1. In `crates/engine/src/types.rs` `MissionState` (additive, `#[serde(default)]`, camelCase): add `pub local_executor_milestones: u32` (if not already added in the escalation feature). This is the denominator: milestones that began under the Local executor tier.

2. In `crates/engine/src/reducer.rs`: in the fold arm for `MilestoneStarted` (the event emitted when a Pending milestone starts — see events.rs ~114 and the run loop in orchestrator.rs), increment `state.local_executor_milestones` when `state.mission.executor_tier == ExecutorTier::Local` at that point. (Escalation flips the tier to Frontier, so milestones started after escalation are correctly not counted as local.) `escalated_milestones` is already folded from `TierEscalated`.

3. Provide the derived rate for consumers: add a method `impl MissionState { pub fn escalation_rate(&self) -> f64 }` returning `escalated_milestones as f64 / local_executor_milestones as f64`, or `0.0` when `local_executor_milestones == 0`. (The dashboard may also derive it from the two counters directly; expose the helper for Rust callers/tests.)

4. Tests: name test functions with substring `escalation_rate`. Fold hand-built event sequences and assert: (a) a mission that starts 2 milestones under Local and escalates once → `local_executor_milestones == 2`, `escalated_milestones == 1`, `escalation_rate() == 0.5`; (b) a mission that never routes local → `local_executor_milestones == 0`, `escalation_rate() == 0.0` (no divide-by-zero); (c) a milestone started AFTER escalation (tier now Frontier) is not counted in the denominator. Use the reducer test harness conventions.

Run fmt/clippy/`cargo test --workspace`. Do not touch the dashboard in this feature.
validationCriteria: `cargo test --workspace escalation_rate 2>&1 | grep -qE 'result: ok\. [1-9]'` passes
2 local milestones + 1 escalation folds to `localExecutorMilestones == 2`, `escalatedMilestones == 1`, `escalation_rate() == 0.5`
A never-local mission yields `localExecutorMilestones == 0` and `escalation_rate() == 0.0` with no panic
Milestones started after escalation (Frontier) are excluded from the denominator; new fields are additive and default to 0 for old logs
fmt/clippy clean; the MissionState JSON served by `mission_state` gains the two camelCase counters automatically

features.title: Mirror the counters in dashboard types and render the escalation rate with a vitest pin
features.spec:
Surface the per-mission escalation rate in the Mission Control UI. Depends on the reducer exposing `localExecutorMilestones`/`escalatedMilestones` on `MissionState`.

1. In `apps/dashboard/src/lib/types.ts` (the CONTRACT MIRROR of `crates/engine/src/types.rs` — keep in sync): add `localExecutorMilestones: number` and `escalatedMilestones: number` to the `MissionState` interface (around lines ~276-288, following the `totalCostUsd` field). Optionally add `executorTier?: 'local' | 'frontier'` on the `Mission` interface if convenient, but the two counters are what the render needs.

2. Render the metric. Follow the existing per-mission stat pattern: `totalCostUsd` is read in `apps/dashboard/src/components/TopBar.tsx` (~line 41, formatted by `fmtCost`) and the progress % is derived in-component in `StatusStrip.tsx` (~lines 64-66). Add an 'Escalation' stat that computes `escalatedMilestones / localExecutorMilestones` (render `0%` / an em-dash when `localExecutorMilestones === 0`) and displays it as a percentage. Put it wherever the per-mission stat row lives (TopBar's stat row is the natural home, mirroring the Usage/Progress stats); add a `fmtPct`-style formatter in `apps/dashboard/src/lib/format.ts` if none exists. Read the fields from the Zustand store `state` (`useKranzStore((s) => s.state)`), consistent with the other stats — do not fetch.

3. Add a vitest pin. Create/extend a colocated `*.test.tsx` for the owning component (e.g. `apps/dashboard/src/components/TopBar.test.tsx`, or extend `StatusStrip.test.tsx`). Its `describe`/`it` name MUST contain the word `escalation` (so `npx vitest run -t escalation` selects it and the contract a6 grep is non-vacuous). Seed the store via `useKranzStore.setState({ state: makeState(...) })` following the factory pattern in `StatusStrip.test.tsx` (~lines 51-111; add `localExecutorMilestones`/`escalatedMilestones` to the `makeState` factory), render the component, and assert the rendered escalation percentage (e.g. a mission with 2 local milestones and 1 escalation renders `50%`, and a never-local mission renders `0%` or `—`).

4. Run the dashboard gate before reporting: `cd apps/dashboard && npx tsc -b && npm run test && npm run build && npm run lint` (deps are already installed in-tree). Keep the embedded bundle in sync if your change requires it (`npm run sync-embedded`/`check-embedded` are part of the full suite). Do not modify the Rust crates in this feature.
validationCriteria: `cd apps/dashboard && npx vitest run -t escalation 2>&1 | grep -qE 'Tests[[:space:]]+[1-9][0-9]* passed'` passes
`cd apps/dashboard && npx tsc -b && npm run test` passes with the new counters mirrored in `types.ts`
A seeded MissionState with `localExecutorMilestones=2, escalatedMilestones=1` renders `50%`; a never-local mission renders `0%` or an em-dash (no NaN/divide-by-zero)
The escalation stat reads from the Zustand store `state`, consistent with `totalCostUsd`/progress; `npm run lint` is clean

consideredAlternatives.chosen: Make `Mission.executor_tier` the single source of truth for the executor's tier. Routing sets it (and the Worker RoleConfig.backend) once at mission seed from the ticket's task-class; escalation flips it via a new additive `tier.escalated` event whose reducer fold resets the Worker backend to frontier. `Engine::select_backend` is left untouched (it already resolves the Worker backend from config), so the whole change lives in the ticket parser, additive type/event fields, the reducer, three cap-site branches in the orchestrator, and the dashboard mirror/render. The validator roles are structurally never consulted for the executor tier, which enforces the deliberately-out-of-scope 'validator stays frontier' guarantee for free.

rejected.approach: Teach `Engine::select_backend(Role::Worker)` to resolve the tier live (tier + configured endpoints → LocalBackend vs Claude) instead of pre-writing config.worker.backend.
rejected.tradeOff: Concentrates behavior in a hot, well-tested selection path with fallback/probe logic, widening blast radius and risking regressions in every worker/validator spawn; the config-source approach keeps select_backend byte-identical.

rejected.approach: Escalate per-feature/per-milestone tier independently (each unit can be local or frontier) rather than one mission-level tier that flips once.
rejected.tradeOff: Turns 'escalation rate per mission' into an ambiguous multi-axis metric and multiplies state and edge cases; the ticket frames the tag and escalation at ticket (mission) granularity, so a single one-way mission tier is simpler and matches the acceptance.

rejected.approach: Add a dedicated escalation-threshold config knob separate from `max_fix_cycles_per_milestone`.
rejected.tradeOff: Introduces a second loop-guard to keep consistent with the existing cap (default 2 == 'two failed validations') and more surface to misconfigure; reusing the existing cap exactly satisfies the spec with no new knob.
